hero.h1: Gas Line Installation in Arlington Heights, IL
hero.sub: Switching to a gas range, adding a grill line on the patio or hooking up a generator. Our licensed plumbers size, run and pressure-test new gas lines across Arlington Heights, with a flat price before we start. From our office on East Central Road.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber inspecting the gas meters and gas line connections in a basement

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.intro: Common projects in Arlington Heights homes:

tiles.body: Many kitchens remodeled from electric to gas need a new line run from the basement.
A gas dryer in a basement laundry room usually needs a short new branch.
A permanent line on the patio means no more propane tanks.
Bigger appliances often need a larger line or a new meter capacity check.

blocks.h2: How We Install a Gas Line

steps.body: We add up the gas load of every appliance so the new line and the existing system can carry it.
We route the pipe, add a shutoff valve at the appliance and connect it with a code-approved connector.
The line is tested for leaks before it's put into service.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Projects in Arlington Heights
blocks.intro: Most homes here were built between 1940 and 1989, so new gas work usually ties into older piping.

items.body: When a postwar kitchen goes from electric to gas, we find the best path from the basement and check that the existing line can handle it.
A natural gas line for a grill or fire pit is a common project in Arlington Heights backyards. We run it safely and add a shutoff outside.
Adding a tankless water heater or a generator can be more than the original pipe was sized for. We check before we connect.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Installation Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: Can my existing gas line handle a new appliance?
items.preview: Sometimes. We calculate the load before we connect anything.
items.answer: Sometimes. We add up the gas demand of everything on the system. If the new appliance would starve others, we upsize the line.

items.q: Do I need a permit for a gas line?
items.preview: New gas work usually requires one. We'll tell you what applies.
items.answer: New gas piping usually requires a permit. We'll tell you what applies to your project when we quote it.

items.q: Can you run a gas line for an outdoor grill?
items.preview: Yes, with a shutoff and a quick-connect outside.
items.answer: Yes. We run the line to the patio, add a shutoff valve and a quick-connect fitting so the grill can be moved safely.

items.q: How long does a gas line installation take?
items.preview: Most are done in a day.
items.answer: Most residential gas line installations are done in a day, including the pressure test. Longer runs or larger lines may take more time.

items.q: Can you move my gas dryer line when I relocate the laundry?
items.answer: Yes. Moving laundry from the basement to the main floor is a common project in Arlington Heights. We run and test the new line and cap the old one.

items.q: How much does gas line installation cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on the length, size and appliance. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on how long the run is, the pipe size and the appliance. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
